chunks.title: Landmark Precedents in Real Estate Law
chunks.content: # Landmark Precedents in Real Estate Law

chunks.title: Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni, (2020) 10 SCC 783
chunks.content:
### Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni, (2020) 10 SCC 783
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (U.U. Lalit, J.)
**Core Holding:** Held that remedies available to allottees/homebuyers under the Consumer Protection Act and RERA are concurrent and mutually complementary. Allottees are not barred from approaching consumer fora even if RERA applies.

chunks.title: Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan, (2019) 5 SCC 725
chunks.content:
### Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan, (2019) 5 SCC 725
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India
**Core Holding:** One-sided standard clauses in builder agreements favoring the developer constitute unfair trade practices; an allottee cannot be compelled to accept delayed possession.

chunks.content: # Procedural Practice Notes — Real Estate & Property

chunks.title: Title Search & RERA Tribunal Practice
chunks.content:
### Title Search & RERA Tribunal Practice
1. **Title Due Diligence:** 30-year chain of title investigation and non-encumbrance certificate from Sub-Registrar office.
2. **RERA Execution:** Execution of RERA refund decrees treated on par with revenue recovery certificate (RRC) arrears.

chunks.title: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (TPA)
chunks.content:
### Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (TPA)
- **Section 53A (Part Performance):** Protection of transferee who has taken possession in furtherance of contract and performed their obligations.
- **Section 54 (Sale of Immovable Property):** Transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised; requires registered instrument for value over ₹100.
- **Section 58 (Mortgages):** Transfer of interest in specific immovable property for securing payment of money advanced.

chunks.title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA)
chunks.content:
### Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA)
- **Section 14 & 18:** Strict promoter liability for failure to deliver possession within stipulated timeline; homebuyer entitled to refund with interest or monthly delay compensation.
